title: Redwood discovery with Vela Analytics - cost/unit economics
summary: Discovery focused on per-token economics, batching/caching levers, and tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Vela provided token/month estimates and budget targets; Redwood team explained batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization impacts, and dedicated-reserved vs hosted pricing. Agreed next steps: send pricing, share benchmark spreadsheet, schedule a technical deep dive for latency SLOs.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private economics
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE. Priya is our SE. Um, we'll spend most of the time on cost/unit economics and how that maps to your token profiles.
[00:12] Jordan Ruiz: Great, thanks. We want to understand whether Hosted makes sense or if we should plan for Dedicated — budget is a hard constraint. We do ~120M tokens/day peak but uneven.
[00:25] Priya Patel: Thanks Jordan. Quick clarifying q — those 120M tokens are generated tokens or include prompts?
[00:30] Maya Singh: That's total tokens in and out, so prompt + generation, avg 350 tokens per call but some longer.
[00:40] Alex Chen: Okay so ballpark 42B tokens/month, with spikes. What's the budget?
[00:46] Samir Patel: We have a stretch budget of $70k/mo and a preferred target of <$50k/mo.
[00:55] Priya Patel: Got it. So quick framing: our hosted API is usage-based per-token; Dedicated gives predictable throughput with reserved GPU capacity and lower per-token unit costs if you commit. Private has similar economics to Dedicated but adds network controls and on-prem costs.
[01:10] Jordan Ruiz: Do you have published per-token numbers? We want rough math.
[01:15] Alex Chen: We do — I'll share the pricing deck after. For the model you mentioned (Llama-like 13B finetuned), hosted list price is roughly $0.0012 per input token and $0.0028 per output token — but that varies by model. For Dedicated, unit costs can drop by 30-60% depending on utilization and batching.
[01:34] Maya Singh: 30-60% is a wide range — what drives the variance?
[01:40] Priya Patel: Main drivers are batch size, KV/prefix cache hit rate, and quantization. If your workload has high repeated prompts we can get high prefix cache hit rates which reduces actual model compute. Also sequence length distribution affects throughput and kernel efficiency.
[01:55] Jordan Ruiz: We have many repeated system prompts and shared prefixes, so caching might be large. How do you measure cache hit rate?
[02:02] Priya Patel: We instrument token-level cache hits in the runtime; typical customers see 10-40% effective reduction in compute from prefix/KV caching, sometimes higher for chat use-cases. We'll run a short benchmark using a sample workload.
[02:15] Alex Chen: Also note that batching increases tokens/sec efficiency — our continuous batching amortizes per-request overhead. With Dedicated you can configure batch latency SLOs; there is a tradeoff between tail latency and batch size.
[02:28] Samir Patel: Latency is important — we need p95 < 400ms for core flows.
[02:32] Priya Patel: Understood. For p95 400ms on a 13B variant, Dedicated with tuned batching is usually reliable. Hosted can also meet that depending on traffic pattern, but for stable p95 at scale Dedicated is common.
[02:45] Jordan Ruiz: Can you share an example cost calc?
[02:47] Alex Chen: Sure — rough calc: if you have 42B tokens/mo and assume 50% of tokens are output, with hosted blended rate of $0.002 per token (weighted), that would be $84k/mo — above your stretch. If Dedicated reduces unit cost by 40% that gets to ~50k/mo assuming good utilization and cache hits.
[03:08] Maya Singh: So Dedicated could hit our target but only if utilization is high. We have variable traffic; bursts could make utilization low.
[03:16] Priya Patel: That's why we recommend autoscaling bursts and a mix: reserve baseline Dedicated for steady-state and use Hosted burst lanes. Our routing supports policy-based fallback between tiers.
[03:28] Jordan Ruiz: Any extra costs for KV cache or prefix caching?
[03:31] Priya Patel: No, caching is part of the runtime. There is memory overhead on nodes; for Dedicated we size pool instances to keep hot KV cache. If you need persistent caching across restarts we can discuss config.
[03:44] Alex Chen: Also quantized model variants (e.g., 4-bit) can reduce GPU throughput cost per token, but may slightly affect output quality — we can recommend quant profiles per workload.
[03:56] Samir Patel: What's the effort to run a benchmark? We can share sample logs and prompts.
[04:00] Priya Patel: 1-2 weeks for a proper bench — we run a synthetic replay over sample traces, measure tokens/sec, p95, cache hit, effective unit cost. We'll need representative prompt set and a small set of queries.
[04:12] Jordan Ruiz: Perfect. Also we have security requirements: VPC peering or Private deployment for restricted data. How does that change cost?
[04:20] Alex Chen: Private deployments include platform fees and often infra costs on your side; dedicated-style economics apply but there is an on-prem or VPC overhead and higher minimum commitments.
[04:30] Maya Singh: We need SOC2 and audit logs.
[04:33] Priya Patel: Redwood supports SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS integrations, and per-request audit logs. I'll share the compliance pack.
[04:45] Jordan Ruiz: Competitors — we've talked to OpenAI and Anthropic. OpenAI hosted looked expensive for our scale; Anthropic had better bulk pricing but limited VPC options.
[04:57] Alex Chen: Understood. We often show customers a modeled TCO comparing per-token hosted, dedicated reserved, and private. We'll include a spread including expected cache hit and quantization scenarios.
[05:08] Maya Singh: What's the commitment length for Dedicated discounts?
[05:12] Alex Chen: Typical commitments are 1/12/36 months with higher discounts for longer. We can model a 12-mo reserved for your baseline.
[05:20] Priya Patel: Also note that warmup/eviction patterns matter — if you scale up new model versions frequently that can reduce effective savings.
[05:28] Jordan Ruiz: Good point. We plan monthly model rollouts.
[05:31] Priya Patel: We'll account for that in the bench.
[05:34] Samir Patel: Any caps or quotas on Hosted? We might hit rate limits.
[05:37] Alex Chen: Hosted has rate limiting and quotas but we can set custom limits for enterprise accounts; Dedicated avoids those limits by design.
[05:44] Maya Singh: Pricing detail request: can you provide per-token example with caching assumptions e.g., no cache, 20% cache, 40% cache and quantized vs unquantized?
[05:55] Alex Chen: Yes, that's exactly what we'll include in the spreadsheet. We'll produce a 3-scenario table.
[06:01] Jordan Ruiz: What's the expected lead time to stand up Dedicated and Private?
[06:05] Priya Patel: Dedicated: 2-6 weeks depending on capacity and network setup. Private (VPC managed) 4-8 weeks; on-prem longer.
[06:13] Samir Patel: Ok. We also want to see tail latency under burst.
[06:17] Priya Patel: We'll include p95/p99 numbers from benchmark and show how batch latency SLO tuning affects tail.
[06:25] Alex Chen: Quick note — we have a public benchmark of a similar 13B workload; I'll link it.
[06:29] Jordan Ruiz: Please share links to pricing deck, benchmark sheet, and compliance docs.
[06:33] Alex Chen: Will do. [shares link] https://redwood.ai/docs/pricing (note: placeholder). Also benchmark spreadsheet: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/vela-bench (placeholder).
[06:45] Maya Singh: For the bench, we will provide a sample one-week traffic trace and 200 representative prompts.
[06:50] Priya Patel: Great, that will be enough.
[06:52] Jordan Ruiz: Any gotchas around tokenization differences altering cost? We use a custom tokenizer post-processing.
[06:58] Priya Patel: Tokenization matters — we'll run a tokenization pass over your prompts to normalize counts. Sometimes models differ ~5-8% tokenization delta.
[07:10] Samir Patel: What's the SLA on Dedicated?
[07:13] Alex Chen: We offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets for Dedicated with enterprise agreements; we'll include the SLA terms in the contract materials.
[07:20] Jordan Ruiz: Alright let's recap and next steps.
[07:22] Alex Chen: Recap: Redwood will run a benchmark on your sample trace, produce a 3-scenario cost model (no cache/20%/40% with quantized variants), share dedicated pricing and compliance docs, and schedule a deep technical session with Priya for p95/p99 tuning.
[07:36] Jordan Ruiz: Sounds good. We'll share the sample data and set up the deep dive; timeline — can you get the pricing and spreadsheet by EOD Fri?
[07:44] Alex Chen: We'll aim for EOD Friday.
[07:46] Maya Singh: Thanks everyone.
[07:48] Priya Patel: Thanks, talk soon.
[07:50] <end of recording>
